prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In frames 1 to 3, the camera wearer looks down at a patterned floor mat where their own bare left knee and two hands (brightest, ~0.3–0.5 m away, within immediate reach) hold food over a small bowl, surrounded by a metal platter of peeled pomegranate on the left (~0.6–0.8 m), a small orange plate in the centre (~0.8 m), a metal pan further ahead (~1.1–1.3 m), the knee and blue bowl of a person on the upper left (~1.0–1.2 m), and the legs and torso of a second person seated on the right (~0.8–1.1 m, about 1 m from the left person) whose upper body and head are cropped out of view. Between frames 3 and 4, the camera wearer turns and tilts their head up and to the left, bringing the left seated person (wearing glasses and a black shirt, ~1.0–1.3 m away, holding a blue bowl of pomegranate seeds in her lap within her arm's reach) fully into the foreground, while a couch (~2.0–3.0 m behind her) and a distant doorway (>3.5 m in the upper right) appear in the background as the right-side person and foreground hands exit the frame. Across frames 4 and 5, the camera shifts slightly further left and upward, making the seated woman appear marginally further down-frame while she faces forward-right toward the absent right-side person rather than looking at the camera wearer. The depth map makes the continuous 3D slant of the floor plane, the vertical relief of the seated people's limbs above the mat, and the ~1–2 m separation between the seated woman and the couch behind her much clearer than the busy patterned RGB image. However, depth is unreliable where thin or low-relief objects like the small red box on the mat and the camera wearer's lower bowl merge into the floor's depth gradient, and in the upper-top regions of frames 1–3 where the sunlit tiled floor behind the mat drops abruptly to pitch black as if at infinite distance.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map partitions the scene into discrete object regions across the 5 frames, separating the floor mat ('dining table') from the camera wearer's lower body and hands ('person' at the bottom of frames 1–3, ~0.3–0.5 m away), the right-side seated person ('person' on the right of frames 1–3, ~0.8–1.1 m away, cropped at the torso), the dishes on the mat (orange centre 'bowl' at ~0.8 m, upper metal 'bowl' at ~1.2 m, upper-left 'bowl' at ~1.0 m, and left platter labelled 'pizza' at ~0.7 m), and in frames 4–5 the woman seated on the left (~1.0–1.3 m away) in front of the background 'couch' (~2.0–3.0 m behind her). It captures the abrupt egocentric viewpoint pan and tilt upward-left between frames 3 and 4 as the camera wearer's own hands, the left platter, and the right-side person disappear off the bottom and right edges, replaced by the full silhouette of the left seated woman facing right and the furniture behind her. While the silhouette masks clearly delineate the boundary between the seated woman's occluding torso and the couch behind her despite busy fabric patterns in RGB, they provide no 3D distance cues or internal head/gaze orientation on their own. The map is heavily unreliable in both class labels and mask consistency: it mislabels the floor mat as 'dining table', the pomegranate platter and seeds as 'pizza', part of the couch behind the woman in frame 4 as 'dog', and a background curtain as 'umbrella'. Furthermore, in frame 3 the right-side person and left platter drop out into unlabelled black voids or merge into the green mat mask, and the bowl right beneath the camera wearer's hands (within 0.4 m reach) is completely missed as a black hole in frames 1–3.
descriptions.pose: In frames 1 to 3, the pose map detects only the magenta 3D hand skeletons of the camera wearer's left and right hands (~0.3–0.5 m in front of and below the head, converging within centimetres of each other over the bowl), and in frame 3 the right hand skeleton drops out entirely even though the hand remains clearly visible in RGB. During frames 1–3, no body or hand keypoints are detected for the partially visible person on the upper left (~1.0–1.2 m away) or the person seated on the right (~0.8–1.1 m away), leaving the spatial layout of the room and surrounding objects completely blank. After the camera wearer turns and tilts their head up and left in frames 4 and 5, a yellow body and facial skeleton appears for the seated woman on the left (~1.0–1.3 m away), showing her shoulders, torso angled forward-right, both arms bent downward with wrists converged in her lap around her bowl (within her immediate reach), and one hip-to-knee segment on the floor. The cluster of facial keypoints (eyes, nose, ears) and shoulder line explicitly trace her head and torso orientation facing to the camera's right—confirming she is looking sideways toward the other person rather than at the camera wearer—and preserve her arm and torso geometry even where her black shirt blends with dark shadows in RGB. However, the pose map is unreliable in omitting her crossed lower legs, failing to generate magenta finger skeletons for her hands holding the bowl in frames 4–5, missing all partial bodies in frames 1–3, and losing the camera wearer's right hand in frame 3.
